punchline: About five of Tim Ferriss's 120 customers were producing around 95 percent of his revenue.
thirty_sec: In The 4-Hour Workweek, Tim Ferriss describes being overwhelmed running his supplement company. Applying the 80/20 principle, he found about 5 of his roughly 120 customers produced around 95 percent of revenue, while a few others caused most of his problems. He dropped or 'fired' the worst, focused on the best, and earned more while working far less. His rule: doing something unimportant well doesn't make it important.
question: Which of your clients or tasks cost you more than they're worth?
